questions.question: Which state of matter has a fixed shape and a fixed volume?
questions.explanation: Solids have fixed shape and volume because their particles are tightly packed in fixed positions.

questions.question: The change of a liquid to a gas is called:
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into a gas; the reverse is condensation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a state of matter?
questions.explanation: Energy is not a state of matter. The three states are solid, liquid and gas.

questions.question: When water vapour cools and turns to liquid water, the process is called:
questions.explanation: Condensation is the change of a gas to a liquid on cooling.

questions.question: Ice at 0°C changes to water. This process is known as:
questions.explanation: Melting is the change of a solid to a liquid at its melting point.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of all living things?
questions.explanation: Reproduction is one of the seven life processes (MRS GREN) shown by all living things.

questions.question: MRS GREN is a way of remembering:
questions.explanation: MRS GREN stands for Movement, Respiration, Sensitivity, Growth, Reproduction, Excretion and Nutrition.

questions.question: The removal of waste products from the body is called:
questions.explanation: Excretion is the removal of metabolic waste products from the body.

questions.question: Which of these is a non-living thing?
questions.explanation: A stone does not carry out any of the life processes, so it is non-living.

questions.question: A car moves and uses fuel, yet it is not a living thing because it cannot:
questions.explanation: Although a car moves and uses fuel, it cannot grow, reproduce or excrete, so it is non-living.

questions.question: Energy is measured in:
questions.explanation: Energy is measured in joules (J); force is measured in newtons.

questions.question: The ultimate source of energy for the Earth is the:
questions.explanation: The sun is the ultimate source of most energy on Earth.

questions.question: A torch converts chemical energy mainly into:
questions.explanation: A torch changes chemical energy into electrical energy, then into light and heat energy.

questions.question: A boy pushes a box with a force of 20 N through 3 m. The work done is:
questions.explanation: Work = Force x Distance = 20 x 3 = 60 J.

questions.question: Which law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed?
questions.explanation: The law of conservation of energy states energy can only change from one form to another.

questions.question: Force is measured using a:
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons using a spring balance.

questions.question: A car travels 240 km in 3 hours. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Speed = distance / time = 240 / 3 = 80 km/h.

questions.question: The force that opposes motion between two surfaces is:
questions.explanation: Friction opposes motion between surfaces and produces heat.

questions.question: A 50 kg student on Earth (g = 10 m/s squared) has a weight of:
questions.explanation: Weight = mass x g = 50 x 10 = 500 N.

questions.question: Which of these is a non-contact force?
questions.explanation: Gravity acts at a distance without contact; the others require contact.

questions.question: The organ that pumps blood round the body is the:
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood round the body.

questions.question: The correct order of organisation in the body is:
questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs and organs form systems.

questions.question: Which system is responsible for breathing?
questions.explanation: The respiratory system (nose, trachea, lungs) is responsible for breathing.

questions.question: The tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach is the:
questions.explanation: The oesophagus (gullet) carries food from the mouth to the stomach.

questions.question: How many bones make up the adult human skeleton?
questions.explanation: The adult human skeleton has 206 bones.
